Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Nature & food

source noun

where something comes from

also origin, source of a river, fountainhead, the root of

classical

Ov. Rem. 97: dē magnīs fontibus orta
Cic. de Or. 1.42: ab illō fonte et capite Sōcrate
Traupman 383: source, fōns, caput
Traupman 206

fōns, fontis m.

noun, third declension

a spring; the source of a river, and of anything

Other words

  • orīgō, orīginis f. — origin, beginning, source

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Varr. LL 5.92: ā pāstōribus enim hōrum vocābulōrum orīgō; Hor. C. 4.14.45: fontium quī cēlat orīginēs Nīlus (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. source, origin

  • caput, capitis n. — the source of a river; the fountainhead

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.10.37 (M-O s.v. source (of river)); Traupman 383

Examples

  • flūmina pauca vidēs dē magnīs fontibus orta: plūrima collēctīs multiplicantur aquīs

    you see few rivers that rise from great sources: most grow by gathering watersOv. Rem. 97–98

  • urgērent praetereā philosophōrum gregēs jam ab illō fonte et capite Sōcrate

    and then the flocks of philosophers would press you, all of them from Socrates on, the fountainhead and sourceCic. de Or. 1.42

See also spring, spring, original, cause, source.
